exposure: Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccine administration (given vs. no vaccine)
Mode of birth (cesarean section vs. vaginal)
outcome: Abundance of bacterial taxa in the intestinal microbiome
Metabolic pathways in the intestinal microbiome
cohort: Healthy, term-born neonates were randomized at birth to receive BCG or no vaccine.
finding: BCG vaccination given in the first few days of life has minimal effect on the composition of the intestinal microbiome at 1 week of age but does influence the abundance of certain metabolic pathways.
mod_finding: The composition of the intestinal microbiome differed between neonates born by cesarean section and vaginally, and specific bacterial taxa varied within both CS and vaginally born neonates based on their BCG vaccination status.
